summary: The solver-visible route control plane is a coupled, production-credible routing domain implementation: ~3,360 lines of reachable Go control logic plus operator UI/config/deployment artifacts exceed the strict-profile floor, with distinct subsystems for FIB tracing, drift/reconcile, transactional apply/rollback, safety, rollout waves, diagnostics, and consistency that interact through shared state and invariants rather than template padding.

evidence.observation: Primary runtime entrypoint exposes 13 core REST routes plus operational and diagnostic route registrars, wiring HTTP workflows to ControlPlane methods.

Central state machine implements preview/apply/rollback with idempotency, per-node transactions, durable JSON persistence, audit sequencing, route/rule mutation validation, and management safety gating.
Policy-aware longest-prefix trace engine evaluates rule priority, lookup tables, ECMP next-hop usability, and route termination types; reused by safety, policy, diagnostics, and path-matrix flows.
Desired-vs-observed drift detection across routes and rules with owned/unowned semantics feeds reconcile, fleet health, impact analysis, and state diff reporting.
Canary-first wave rollout executes per-node observed-state transitions with offline failure handling, revision checks, and durable rollout records.
Candidate change safety combines management-path tracing, protected-CIDR blackhole checks, link presence, and gateway-on-link validation before permitting mutations.
Topology and dependency graph builders derive link health, unreachable gateways, and cycle detection across routes, rules, and interfaces.
Multi-check diagnostics aggregate node heartbeat, management path, observed revision skew, per-table route integrity, rule/table references, link usage, audit monotonicity, and recovery blocking.

Cross-fleet consistency scans detect duplicate hostnames/addresses, route identity collisions, rule priority conflicts, transaction/idempotency mismatches, rollout duplication, and audit counter drift.
Operator dashboard exercises preview/apply, reconcile, and rollout APIs against live revision state, confirming end-to-end workflow reachability beyond thin HTTP glue.
Build entrypoint compiles routecp binary, materializes runtime directories, and documents starter defect injection at build time while preserving solver-visible source contracts.
Representative multi-site edge fleet with IPv4/IPv6 routes, multipath, down links, and policy-table indirection provides domain-realistic state samples even though runtime seeding is API-driven.
Task metadata declares advanced systems profile with separate verifier environment, 8192MB runtime, and /app/routecp workdir aligned to the control-plane artifact surface.

do_not_change: Core ControlPlane transaction, persistence, and audit model in internal/controlplane/controlplane.go
Shared traceState FIB/policy lookup hub in internal/controlplane/fib.go
Cross-module safety, drift ownership, and rollout wave invariants that create partial-fix traps
HTTP route surface partitioning between core, operational, and diagnostic entrypoints
next_gate: QUALITY_INTERLOCK completion pending parallel Q4 PASS; then Pre-LLMaJ aggregate

role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: ~3,364 lines of Go control-plane/runtime logic across 20 modules, plus ~260 lines operator UI (web/app.ts), ~126 lines fleet reference config, ~124 lines Ansible deployment workflow, and Dockerfile build/entrypoint (~35 lines). Total solver-visible runtime/config surface ~3,900 lines, above the 3,000-line strict-profile floor; bulk is branching domain logic rather than comments or generated/vendor code.
MAJOR_MODULES: controlplane.go — revisioned desired state, preview/apply/rollback transactions, idempotency, durable persistence, audit
domain.go — route/rule/link types, canonicalization, identity keys, normalization
fib.go — policy-ordered trace, LPM route selection, ECMP usability, route-table summaries
drift.go + state_diff.go — desired/observed equivalence, owned drift filtering, reconcile transactions
rollout.go + fleet.go + change_window.go — selector/canary wave planning, fleet health aggregation, failure-domain-aware change windows
safety.go + policy.go + impact.go — management reachability, protected CIDR checks, policy findings, blast-radius scoring
topology.go + route_analysis.go — link/gateway health, dependency cycles, route shadowing, ECMP degradation
diagnostics.go + recovery.go + consistency.go — operational health matrix, non-terminal transaction recovery, cross-object invariant scans
cmd/routecp/* + web/app.ts — HTTP/API and dashboard operator workflows
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Restoring canonicalPrefix masking without restoring routeIdentity table component breaks duplicate-route detection while appearing to fix prefix formatting alone
Re-enabling Apply idempotency or base-revision checks without restoring offline-node guards yields locally green applies that violate fleet safety
Fixing drift reconcile ownership filtering without observed-revision conflict handling can hide unmanaged external drift
Patching rollout wave-size or canary validation independently can pass canary ordering tests while leaving stale-node short-circuit bugs
Adding management-path checks in Preview without link/gateway validation in CheckSafety allows unsafe candidates to pass preview-only workflows
Repairing validateDesired node references without priority-collision enforcement permits conflicting policy tables to appear valid
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Removing ~25% of solver-visible core (e.g., fib.go trace engine plus drift/reconcile and rollout wave executors) would eliminate management reachability enforcement, policy-aware forwarding analysis, owned drift reconciliation, and staged fleet rollouts—collapsing most cross-module invariants and operator safety workflows rather than cosmetic dead code.
role_output.REQUIRED_CHANGES: None for production-logic acceptance at current scope.
